_about.idea: The technology tree of the grand campaign. Five branches, four steps deep. A nation's research teams each work on one technology at a time; a technology takes 'months' of one team's work, can be started once everything in 'needs' is researched, and takes 'early' longer for every year it is begun before its 'year'. The historical scenarios do not use the tree: there, research runs on history's clock (research.json).
_about.effects: 'field' raises one of the eight branches of research.json by a level for good, worth that branch's 'per' wherever the branch counts (tanks, infantry weapons, doctrine, fighters, bombers, navy, radar, war production). 'unlock' lists the orders that cannot be placed without the technology ('corps:arm', 'corps:mot', 'ship:cv', 'para'). 'slots' adds research teams. 'winterKit' ends the eastern winter's penalty for the nation's troops. 'sealift' adds shipping for that many more corps a month. 'attack', 'defence' with 'when', 'drafts', 'cost', 'fleet' and 'seaLoss' work exactly as they do for a national ability in traits.json.
_about.start: What each nation has researched when the war begins. A campaign begun in a later year gives every nation the months of research in between, chosen as its own staff would.
_about.slots: Research teams each nation begins with.
_about.units: Formations the tree unlocks beyond the ordinary kinds: 'para' is an airborne corps, raised like infantry, 'most' at once in the field and on order.
_about.ai: How a computer-run nation chooses: the lowest of step times 'tier', plus the branch's place in its order of preference times 'branch', plus 'early' for every year a technology is ahead of its time, less 'teams' for one that adds a research team, plus 'later' for one in 'skip' (what a computer-run nation has no use for, taken only when nothing else is open), less 'fuel' for one that makes oil while the nation's stock of it is running down (the months in resources.json). 'order' is each nation's preference among the branches.

branches.label: Land
branches.text: Tanks, guns and the infantry's weapons.

branches.label: Air
branches.text: Fighters, bombers and the radar that guides them.

branches.label: Naval
branches.text: Fleets, convoys and landings from the sea.

branches.label: Industry
branches.text: Factories, manpower and the laboratories themselves.

branches.label: Doctrine
branches.text: How the army is taught to fight.

techs.name: Anti-tank guns
techs.text: Light, low guns that travel with the infantry and can stop a tank at close range.

techs.name: Tank arm
techs.text: Tanks gathered into divisions of their own, with the workshops, fuel columns and radio sets that keep them moving.

techs.name: Motorised infantry
techs.text: Infantry carried in lorries, able to keep up with the tanks and hold what they take.

techs.name: Medium tanks
techs.text: A tank with a gun that can fight other tanks and armour the light guns of 1939 cannot pierce.

techs.name: Heavy artillery
techs.text: Long-range guns and heavy howitzers, worked to a single fire plan.

techs.name: Submachine guns and mortars
techs.text: Firepower a platoon can carry: more automatic weapons, and mortars of its own.

techs.name: Heavy tanks
techs.text: Thick armour and a gun that outranges anything it meets, at the price of weight, fuel and factory hours.

techs.name: Rocket artillery
techs.text: Batteries of rockets on lorries: a whole regiment's weight of fire in half a minute, then gone before the reply.

techs.name: Tank destroyers
techs.text: Heavy guns on tracks: cheap to build, hard to see and deadly from ambush.

techs.name: Assault rifles
techs.text: One weapon with the reach of a rifle and the fire of a machine pistol, in every rifleman's hands.

techs.name: Late-war armour
techs.text: Sloped plate, a long gun and wide tracks in one design, built in thousands.

techs.name: Monoplane fighters
techs.text: All-metal fighters with enclosed cockpits, retracting wheels and a battery of guns in the wings.

techs.name: Medium bombers
techs.text: Fast twin-engined bombers with trained navigators and a proper bombsight.

techs.name: Early-warning radar
techs.text: A chain of stations that sees a raid forming up while it is still far out.

techs.name: Close air support
techs.text: Dive bombers and fighter-bombers on call to the spearheads, with air force officers riding in the lead columns.

techs.name: Long-range fighters
techs.text: Drop tanks and thrifty engines take the fighters all the way to the target and back.

techs.name: Four-engined bombers
techs.text: Heavy bombers that carry tons where the mediums carried hundredweights.

techs.name: Fighter control
techs.text: Controllers on the ground steer each fighter onto its target by radar, by day or by night.

techs.name: Jet fighters
techs.text: No propeller, and a hundred miles an hour faster than anything else in the sky.

techs.name: Guided weapons
techs.text: Bombs steered onto the target by radio after they leave the aircraft.

techs.name: Sonar and convoys
techs.text: Escorts that can hear a submerged boat, and merchant ships sailing together under their guard.

techs.name: Ocean-going submarines
techs.text: Boats with the range to hunt far out on the trade routes, built to one standard pattern.

techs.name: Carrier aviation
techs.text: Deck landing, folding wings and the trained crews to fly aircraft from a ship at sea.

techs.name: Landing craft
techs.text: Flat-bottomed craft with bow ramps that put men and tanks straight onto an open beach.

techs.name: Radar gunnery
techs.text: The guns find their range by radar, in darkness and through smoke.

techs.name: Escort groups
techs.text: Escorts trained to hunt as teams, with small carriers to close the gap in mid-ocean.

techs.name: Prefabricated ships
techs.text: Hulls welded together from sections built inland, launched in weeks.

techs.name: Carrier task forces
techs.text: Fast carriers, battleships and their screen sailing and fighting as one body.

techs.name: Machine tools
techs.text: Modern lathes, presses and gauges, and the skilled hands to set them.

techs.name: Research institutes
techs.text: Scientists and engineers brought together from the universities and set to war work.

techs.name: Assembly lines
techs.text: Tanks, lorries and aircraft built on a moving line from standard parts.

techs.name: General mobilisation
techs.text: Every class called up in its turn, with the depots and instructors to turn recruits into replacements.

techs.name: Synthetic fuel and rubber
techs.text: Petrol from coal and rubber from the chemical works, so the tanks and the factories do not wait on cargoes.

techs.name: War economy
techs.text: One central plan for steel, labour and machine tools, and nothing made that the war does not need.

techs.name: Hydrogenation plants
techs.text: Great works beside the coalfields that turn brown coal into aviation spirit by the trainload.

techs.name: Central laboratories
techs.text: The institutes joined under one directorate with first call on money and men.

techs.name: Mass production
techs.text: Simplified designs turned out round the clock by factories that make one thing only.

techs.name: Staff colleges
techs.text: Officers trained to one method, so that an order means the same thing to everyone who reads it.

techs.name: Defence in depth
techs.text: Belt behind belt of positions, with reserves placed to strike back at whatever breaks in.

techs.name: Mobile warfare
techs.text: The fast troops massed at one point, sent through and kept moving, with the infantry to follow.

techs.name: Mountain warfare
techs.text: Pack guns, mule trains and men who can climb with a full load.

techs.name: Airborne forces
techs.text: Parachute and glider troops, and the transport aircraft to deliver them behind an enemy coast.

techs.name: Winter equipment
techs.text: Padded uniforms, felt boots, oils that do not freeze and engines that start in the cold.

techs.name: Battle groups
techs.text: Tanks, infantry, guns and engineers put together for the task in hand under whoever is on the spot.

techs.name: Amphibious assault
techs.text: Navy, army and air force rehearsed to one timetable, from the bombardment to the beach.

techs.name: Deep operations
techs.text: Whole armies fed through a breach one behind another, aimed at what lies far behind the front.

para.label: Airborne corps
para.blurb: Parachute and glider troops. Once a month they can be dropped on an enemy coast across one sea with no ships at all, as long as the enemy's fighters do not hold the sky there. They land without heavy weapons, so pick a weakly held target.
